about: Drop-in PATCH.DLL (Phase 3a, a replacement TIMER.DLL before 2026-11-15): where it patches the player's own v2.25 WINRACE.EXE in memory, and the code it must leave untouched. Checksums only, no game bytes. sha256 values are recorded by 'python3 brr.py dropin-build' from work/game/WINRACE.EXE and checked on every build; the DLL checks them again at run time before patching anything.

sites.name: vga_wait_retrace
sites.patch: JMP to brr_hook_retrace: waits for the next 1/70 s instead of reading VGA port 0x3DA (privileged on Windows NT and Wine)

sites.name: clock_read
sites.patch: run_screen_frame: MOV EAX,[import _TIMER_Count]; MOV AX,[EAX] -> CALL brr_hook_clock_read + 3 NOP (count from QueryPerformanceCounter at the moment of reading; frame pacing)

sites.name: cap_compare
sites.patch: run_screen_frame: CMP AL,0x23 -> CMP AL,cap

sites.name: cap_store
sites.patch: run_screen_frame: MOV byte [frame_ticks],0x23 -> cap

sites.name: race_tick_callback
sites.patch: WndProc: MOV EDX,race_tick -> brr_hook_race_tick (calls race_tick, then snapshots vehicles)

sites.name: race_tick_compare
sites.patch: run_screen_frame PrtSc check: CMP ESI,race_tick -> brr_hook_race_tick, so the race screenshot routine is still chosen

sites.name: race_draw_callback
sites.patch: WndProc: MOV EBX,race_draw -> brr_hook_race_draw (writes interpolated vehicles, calls race_draw, restores)

sites.name: approach_clamped
sites.patch: MOV AL,[frame_ticks] -> MOV AL,1; NOP x3 (step per tick, not per tick x ticks-per-frame)

sites.name: camera_mode4_previous
sites.patch: MOV AX,[ESI+0x10]; MOV word [ESI+0x24],0; MOV [ESI+0x46],AX -> MOV word [ESI+0x24],0; CALL brr_hook_cam4; NOP x3 (stores 'previous' only when a tick ran)

sites.name: camera_update_call
sites.patch: render_view: CALL camera_update -> CALL brr_hook_camera_update (calls camera_update, then for drawing only recomputes the follow camera's roll over 7 ticks and applies camera smoothing; the game's values are restored after the draw)

sites.name: rotation_builder
sites.patch: FUN_00446670 (the 3D engine's rotation-matrix builder; drawing only, not reachable from the race tick): first 5 bytes (PUSH EDI; PUSH ESI; SHR EAX,5) -> JMP brr_hook_rotation. During the race draw with fine_angles, brr_rotation_fine builds the matrix from full 16-bit angles (bit-identical at multiples of 64); otherwise a trampoline repeats those three instructions and jumps to 0x446675, so the original runs

sites.name: present_window_call
sites.patch: The DirectDraw present (0x42CE78) calls the windowed blit 0x42CD2C here (CALL rel32). With [clock] vsync=1 (and cnc-ddraw not pacing), the call goes to brr_hook_present_window, which waits for the vertical blank (IDirectDraw::WaitForVerticalBlank) and then continues into 0x42CD2C

sites.name: display_choice
sites.patch: WinMain's colour-depth test (CMP EDI,8; JZ 0x40112A) -> CALL brr_hook_display_choice, which continues WinMain at 0x40112A (windowed), 0x401114 (full screen, as if the 256-colour question was answered OK) or 0x4010EE (the original question), by [display] mode

sites.name: present_entry
sites.patch: The DirectDraw present's first instructions (PUSH EBX; PUSH ECX; PUSH EDX; CMP byte [0x52D720],0) -> JMP brr_hook_present + 5 NOPs. In a window on a desktop that isn't 256 colours, brr_present_gdi draws the 8-bit frame buffer with StretchDIBits and returns 1; otherwise a trampoline repeats the four instructions and continues at 0x42CE82

sites.name: playback_tick_callback
sites.patch: WndProc, screen 0x83 (Load Recording): MOV EDX,0x413400 (its tick) -> brr_hook_playback_tick (before/after tick hooks, as the race's)

sites.name: playback_draw_callback
sites.patch: WndProc, screen 0x83 (Load Recording): MOV EBX,0x4131DC (its draw) -> brr_hook_playback_draw (writes interpolated vehicles, draws, restores)

sites.name: joystick_call
sites.patch: run_screen_frame's CALL joystick_to_keys (0x41A950) -> CALL brr_hook_joystick: with [controller] enabled and an XInput pad connected, the pad's state is written into the game's joystick variables (0x44B9CA/CC/D6, calibration 0x44B9E4), then joystick_to_keys runs unchanged

sites.name: menu_hotspots_call
sites.patch: run_screen_frame's per-tick CALL menu_hotspots_tick (0x427E28) -> CALL brr_hook_menu_hotspots, which runs it unchanged between brr_before_menu_hotspots and brr_after_menu_hotspots (src/dropin/keys.c). With [fixes] menu_keys, a key that has fired a menu action is hidden from that call (and only that call) until it is released or pressed afresh, so one press fires one action; [debug] log_keys logs the keyboard

sites.name: scn_commit_call
sites.patch: scn_load (0x4200F0, a screen's .SCN script): CALL menu_hotspot_commit (0x427FAC) -> CALL brr_hook_scn_commit: the commit as before, then a key hotspot for Esc (0x01) or left or right (0x4B/0x6B, 0x4D/0x6D) is noted for a twin on joystick 1's button 2 (0x74) or stick (0x77, 0x78) (keys.c; not on the keys screen 0x0E or the joystick screen 0x17)

sites.name: scn_end_call
sites.patch: scn_load's last call, CALL menu_background_save (0x412EAC) -> CALL brr_hook_scn_end: the noted twins added after the script's own hotspots (scripts refer to theirs by number), then menu_background_save

sites.name: version_date
sites.patch: FUN_00406330 (main menu version text, "%s%s %s"): PUSH 0x44DA0C (the date "(09-05-96)") -> our "FIX<version>", so the menu reads V2.24WR FIX0.2.0

sites.name: version_number
sites.patch: FUN_00406330 (main menu version text): PUSH 0x44DA1C ("V2.24", never updated for the v2.25 patch; the game's own "V2.25" is only on the network dialog) -> our "V2.25", so the menu reads V2.25WR FIX<version> (director, 2026-11-10)

sites.name: credit_lookup_call
sites.patch: The main menu's credits ticker (0x4234D8, every 128 ticks): CALL 0x42818C (the language text lookup of "CRED_<n>", n from the counter 0x44BCE0) -> CALL brr_hook_credit_lookup: at step 2, after the publisher's and the developer's lines, our own line ("Camera / Modern Windows fix by ctrl-alt-rees", director 2026-11-14), and after it CRED_<n-1>, so every one of the game's 28 lines still shows, in order

sites.name: credit_count
sites.patch: The credits ticker's MOV EBX,0x1C (the counter wraps at 28 lines) -> 0x1D: 29 steps, the game's 28 lines and ours

sites.name: window_command_66
sites.patch: WndProc's WM_COMMAND dispatch, command 0x66 (from full screen to a window; Tab in full screen): JBE 0x40235D -> JBE 0x402619 (DefWindowProcA, as for an unknown command). The switch breaks the window (director, 2026-11-10)

sites.name: window_command_67
sites.patch: WndProc's WM_COMMAND dispatch, command 0x67 (from a window to full screen; Tab in a window, or the Modes menu's Full screen): JBE 0x4023B6 -> JBE 0x402619 (DefWindowProcA)

sites.name: window_command_resolution
sites.patch: WndProc's WM_COMMAND dispatch, commands 0x64 and 0x65 (low and high resolution: keypad - and +, the Modes menu): JBE 0x4021B9; JMP 0x40228B -> JMP 0x402619 (DefWindowProcA) + 2 NOPs. Modern renderer only, which chooses the picture's size itself (the director's renderer split, 2026-11-15); the original renderer keeps both, as in 1996

sites.name: class_menu
sites.patch: window_register_class: MOV [ESP+0x24],EDI (WNDCLASS lpszMenuName = 'AppMenu_' + language) -> MOV [ESP+0x24],ESI (0): no menu bar on the window. Modern renderer only, whose game runs full screen, in cnc-ddraw's window when windowed (the director's renderer split, 2026-11-15)

sites.name: set_menu_call
sites.patch: WndProc's CALL [SetMenu] (after LoadMenuA of AppMenu_<language>) -> CALL brr_set_menu; NOP x2: removes the Modes menu's items 0x66 and 0x67, then calls SetMenu

sites.name: language_start
sites.patch: WinMain, before the config is read and before any screen or menu: MOV EAX,[0x44D858] ("ENG", stored as the language at 0x44AFF4) -> MOV EAX,[our code], the launcher's [display] language

sites.name: language_config
sites.patch: The config reader (0x40F09C), case 2 (lang): MOV EDX,0x44AFF4 -> our scratch buffer, so DEFAULT.CFG and the players' own .CFG files (loaded after name entry) don't override the launcher's language; the in-game Language menu still works for the session

sites.name: resolution_display
sites.patch: Data: the display size the game starts with, 320x200 -> 640x480, before WinMain. The window (0x401390), DirectDraw (0x42C590, called from 0x42405A) and every screen's set-up read it, so the game starts in its high-resolution mode, as after menu command 0x65 (keypad +)

sites.name: resolution_frame
sites.patch: Data: the frame's width, height and size, 320, 200, 64000 -> 640, 480, 307200 (command 0x65 sets the same)

sites.name: menu_double_call
sites.patch: 0x426358: CALL 0x4262B4 (the menus' doubling into the middle of a 640x480 frame) -> 5 NOP; the new renderer enlarges the 320x200 menu by whole numbers into the final picture instead (render.c)

sites.name: menu_mouse
sites.patch: 0x4274FC's mapping of the mouse into the menu (only at exactly 640x480: x / 2, (y - 40) / 2) -> CALL brr_hook_menu_mouse (the inverse of the new renderer's layout: (x - left) / across, (y - top) / down) + JMP to its stores + NOPs

sites.name: view_max
sites.patch: Experimental, [display] render_resolution=max with the new renderer. The view record's maximum width and height (words 640, 480), from which the 3D engine (0x440610) allocates its 8-bit picture, 16-bit depth buffer and row table on its first call -> 1008, 756 (RENDER_MAX_W, RENDER_MAX_H), before WinMain

sites.name: sprite_scale_rows
sites.patch: Experimental, Max. sprite_draw_scaled (0x426F90, the HUD's sprites): MOV EDX,EBX; MOV EAX,EBX; SAR EDX,31; SUB EAX,EDX; SAR EAX,1 (the rows' error start, drawn height / 2) -> CALL brr_hook_sprite_rows (thunks.asm): max(drawn / 2, drawn - sprite height). Drawn more than twice as big (views wider than 1,280 pixels), the game's start reads one row past the sprite (the next sprite's size bytes showed as green specks under the map); up to twice the size the value is the game's own

sites.name: sprite_scale_columns
sites.patch: Experimental, Max. sprite_draw_scaled: MOV EAX,ESI; SUB EAX,EDX; SAR EAX,1 (the columns' error start, drawn width / 2; EDX is the width's sign from 0x427190) -> CALL brr_hook_sprite_columns: max(drawn / 2, drawn - sprite width), as sprite_scale_rows

sites.name: hud_draw_call
sites.patch: render_view: CALL hud_draw (0x423658) -> CALL brr_hook_hud_draw (thunks.asm): the view's size set to 320x200, the high-resolution flag cleared and the 2D routines' buffer (0x542030) pointed at our layers around it, so the game draws its 320x200 HUD (GAMEVGA.SPR, the 64x64 map) there instead of into the 3D view; hud.c lays the layers over the composed race picture, enlarged by whole numbers and pinned to its corners. Modern renderer, single view; split screen and the screenshot's redraw keep the game's own

sites.name: hud_icon_call
sites.patch: render_view: CALL hud_draw_playback_icon (0x4236F0, recordings' playback) -> CALL brr_hook_hud_icon: the same, into the same frame's layers

sites.name: sprite_scaled_entry
sites.patch: sprite_draw_scaled's first instructions (PUSH ESI; PUSH EDI; PUSH EBP; SUB ESP,0x50) -> JMP brr_hook_sprite_scaled: while the HUD draws into our layers, brr_hud_sprite picks the layer of the sprite's corner from its caller (the map left; place, nitro and laps right; damage and messages centred; top or bottom by y); then those instructions and on from 0x426F96. Every caller of sprite_draw_scaled is HUD drawing or the demo's goodbye screen (bye_*), which the flag leaves alone

sites.name: proj_scale_store
sites.patch: set_view: MOV [0x542000],EAX (the horizontal projection scale, width x 256 / 320; the vertical one follows from it) -> CALL brr_hook_proj_scale (thunks.asm): for a widescreen race view, height x 16 / 15 instead (the scale of the 4:3 view as tall), so the view shows as much from top to bottom as 4:3 and more at the sides. Native widescreen only ([display] widescreen with Max, full screen on a screen wider than 4:3)

sites.name: landscape_width
sites.patch: landscape_setup: MOV EDX,EAX; MOV EBX,10; SAR EDX,31; IDIV EBX (7 x vision / 10, the visible ground's half-width - 1 at its far edge, for 4:3) -> CALL brr_hook_landscape_width (thunks.asm) and NOPs: the same division, then brr_landscape_width (render.c) widens it by the view's shape against 4:3, as far as the 64x64 grid holds (far corners within 31 cells). Native widescreen only

sites.name: project_x
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. model_op_vertices: IMUL EAX,[0x542000]; CDQ (x x the horizontal scale in 32 bits, then sign-extended for IDIV by the depth) -> CALL brr_project_x (thunks.asm) and 3 NOPs: IMUL dword ptr [0x542000], the product in EDX:EAX, counting the ones that wouldn't fit 32 bits. x is view space x 256, so the 32-bit product overflowed for corners more than about 10.7 squares to the side at 1,440 rows (32 at 640x480): the corner landed anywhere on screen, a spike across the picture. The quotient stays within 3.4 million (x < 2^23, the scale < 6,600, the depth >= 16,384), so the IDIV can't overflow

sites.name: project_y
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. model_op_vertices: IMUL EAX,[0x542004]; CDQ -> CALL brr_project_y and 3 NOPs, as project_x for y

sites.name: backface_model
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. poly_cull_outcodes (model polygons): IMUL EAX,EDX; SUB EDI,EBX; MOV EBX,[ESI+0xC]; SUB EBX,ECX; IMUL EDI,EBX; SUB EDI,EAX (the screen cross product, 32 bits) -> CALL brr_backface (thunks.asm) and NOPs: the same in 64 bits, its sign for the JS after. With corners far off screen the 32-bit product's sign was wrong: faces dropped or back faces drawn

sites.name: backface_polygon
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. poly_cull_visible (engine_draw_polygon's polygons): the same as backface_model

sites.name: clip_x_t
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. clip_edge_x: SHL EAX,16; NEG ECX; JZ; CDQ; IDIV ECX; MOV [ESI+0x10],EBX; MOV ECX,EAX (the fraction of the edge at the screen's left or right edge, from (x0 - edge) << 16 in 32 bits) -> CALL brr_clip_t_x and NOPs: the dividend in 64 bits. Wrong beyond 32,767 pixels off screen

sites.name: clip_x_lerp
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. clip_edge_x: IMUL EAX,ECX; SAR EAX,16 ((y1 - y0) x the fraction, 32 bits) -> IMUL ECX; SHRD EAX,EDX,16, as the game interpolates the depth just after

sites.name: clip_y_t
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. clip_edge_y: as clip_x_t for the top and bottom edges (MOV [ESI+0xC],EBX) -> CALL brr_clip_t_y

sites.name: clip_y_lerp
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. clip_edge_y: as clip_x_lerp, for x

sites.name: cull_margin
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] precise_3d. object_cull_sphere: SHL dword ptr [0x54B498],7 (the radius x 128, the margin for the screen-edge tests, against x x the projection scale) -> CALL brr_cull_margin and NOPs: the radius x the larger scale. x 128 was half the radius at 320 wide and a twelfth at 1,440 rows: objects vanished at the screen's sides while mostly still in view

sites.name: unlit_restore_6
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] object_lighting. display_list_draw, node type 6 (effects: dust, smoke, drawn unlit): CMP DI,2; JNZ; PUSH 2; CALL engine_set_shading (put back the near objects' smooth lighting only once the list had reached them) -> CALL brr_shading_restore and NOPs: mode 2 then, else 1. The game left the engine unlit, so far objects drawn after an effect came out unlit, flickering bright and lit as dust came and went

sites.name: unlit_restore_9
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] object_lighting. display_list_draw, node type 9 (also drawn unlit): as unlit_restore_6; the JNZ's target is the JMP that follows

sites.name: shading_threshold
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] object_shading smooth or flat. display_list_draw's start: MOV EBP,[0x44B044]; SUB EBP,9; XOR EDI,EDI; clamp EBP to 3-8 (the distance in squares inside which objects get smooth vertex lighting; flat face lighting beyond) -> CALL brr_hook_shading_threshold (thunks.asm; EBP from brr_shading_threshold, render.c: 4,096 every object smooth, -4,096 none), XOR EDI,EDI and NOPs

sites.name: lod_select
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] object_detail matched (the default) or highest. object_draw: CMP dword ptr [0x54B488],0 (the object's depth, 16.16, before the level-of-detail loop; ESI the model's table of (depth, offset) pairs ended by -1) -> CALL brr_hook_lod (thunks.asm) and 2 NOPs: brr_lod_select (render.c) sets brr_lod_depth (the depth x 512 / the horizontal scale: the depth the object would have in the game's 640-wide picture; or 0, the most detailed), then the same CMP for the JS after

sites.name: lod_compare
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] object_detail. object_draw's level-of-detail loop: CMP ECX,[0x54B488] -> CMP ECX,[brr_lod_depth]: the model's level by the depth it would have in the game's 640-wide picture. At 1600x900 widescreen (scale 960) an object at the same depth is 1.9 times bigger than at 640x480: fences switched from their thin far model to the thick near one close up, and objects vanished at their last level nearer than they looked

sites.name: fit_depth
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] object_detail. scenery_fit_lods_to_ground (0x42B6EC; ground-hugging scenery such as wooden fences, fitted to the ground just before they're drawn): XOR EAX,EAX; MOV AX,[ECX+0x22] where its two branches meet, ESI the object's centre depth -> CALL brr_hook_fit_depth (thunks.asm) and a NOP: ESI the depth as the level-of-detail choice sees it (brr_lod_scale), then the same two instructions. It fits only the versions whose distance band holds the depth, so with matched detail the version drawn hadn't been fitted to the spot: fences leant at odd angles, twitching, until the game's own depth reached its band

sites.name: if_distance_depth
sites.patch: Modern renderer, [display] object_detail. model_op_if_distance (model opcode 15, the models' own 'if nearer than' tests, which choose detailed parts such as the armco barriers' high-resolution texture): MOV ECX,[0x54B488] -> MOV ECX,[brr_lod_depth], the depth object_draw's level-of-detail choice has just worked out for the same object (site lod_select), so the models' parts switch where their versions do

sites.name: record_init_base
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). display_list_init (start-up and each level's reset): MOV EDX,0x4CA430, the first landscape record -> brr_records (distance.c, 8,192 records of 0xBD bytes), so the game prepares ours (type 7, two 3-point triangles)

sites.name: record_init_end
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). display_list_init: CMP EDX,0x5268C0, the records' end before the loop -> the end of ours

sites.name: record_init_loop
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). display_list_init: the same CMP at the loop's end -> the end of ours

sites.name: record_rewind
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). display_list_rewind (each landscape walk): MOV EDX,0x4CA430 -> brr_records

sites.name: record_limit
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). landscape_walk: CMP EDX,0x523980 (stop when the next column might not fit: 64 records short of 2,000) -> 64 short of our 8,192. At 44 squares in 16:9 the game's 1,936 were 93% full; 60 squares needs about 3,400

sites.name: node_first
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). display_list_clear (each view): MOV ECX,0x5268D1, the first object node -> brr_nodes (distance.c, 8,192 nodes of 17 bytes instead of 999)

sites.name: node_hint
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). display_list_rewind: MOV [0x52D6EC],0x5268D1 (the cells' insertion hint: the first node) -> brr_nodes

sites.name: node_limit_after_last
sites.patch: Modern renderer ([display] big_lists, always with it). display_list_add_after_last: CMP ...,0x52AB28 (the object nodes' end: 999 nodes) -> the end of brr_nodes (8,192). Seen 157 at most at 25 squares; objects out to 60 need about 900

sites.name: object_radius_vision
sites.patch: Modern renderer, max_draw_distance above 25. render_view: MOV EAX,[0x44B044] (the vision distance, for the radius objects and other vehicles are gathered within: isqrt(vision^2 + (camera height / 512)^2) squares) -> brr_object_vision (patch.c: the far distance), so trees, buildings and vehicles are drawn as far as the ground; the vision distance stays 25 for the near pass. Their distance fade (display_list_draw) already follows the far distance

sites.name: set_view_entry
sites.patch: Experimental, [display] render_resolution=max with the new renderer. set_view's first instructions (PUSH EBX; PUSH ECX; PUSH ESI; MOV ESI,EDX) -> JMP brr_hook_set_view: brr_view_size (render.c) turns the single-view 640x480 race view (split-screen flag 0x44BE74 clear) into the biggest 4:3 view up to 1008x756 that fills the final picture best by a whole number; every other size passes through; then set_view runs as before from 0x425F7D

sites.name: screenshot_race_call
sites.patch: With set_view_entry (Max) or the smooth sky. run_screen_frame's race screenshot (PrtSc, key-table index 0x54): CALL 0x423B5C -> CALL brr_hook_screenshot_race: with the race drawn bigger than 640x480, the view goes back to 640x480 for the screenshot (its PCX writer 0x4239BC packs each row into a 1,280-byte stack buffer, enough for 640 pixels only) and to ours afterwards

sites.name: screenshot_tape_call
sites.patch: With set_view_entry (Max) or the smooth sky. run_screen_frame's numbered TAPEDECK screenshot: CALL 0x423C40 -> CALL brr_hook_screenshot_tape, as screenshot_race_call

sites.name: dd_setup_entry
sites.patch: The DirectDraw set-up's first 4 instructions (PUSH ESI; PUSH EDI; PUSH EBP; SUB ESP,0x84) -> JMP brr_hook_dd_setup + 4 NOP: in full screen the mode becomes the screen's own size (the new renderer), then those instructions, and on at 0x42C599

sites.name: dd_mode_check
sites.patch: The set-up's full-screen size check (320x200 -> cooperative level 0x51, 640x480 -> 0x11, else 'Invalid full screen size') from its 640x480 test -> JMP 0x42C782 (level 0x11, DDSCL_EXCLUSIVE | DDSCL_FULLSCREEN) + NOPs, so the screen's own size is accepted

sites.name: dd_mode_bpp
sites.patch: dd_setup's SetDisplayMode bits per pixel (the immediate of PUSH 0x8 at 0x42C7D7) -> 0x20: full colour in full screen; render.c composes the 32-bit picture straight into the back surface and flips, instead of the game's 8-bit copy, and clears dd_palette_pending (0x44BFC4), as a 32-bit surface takes no palette

sites.name: sky_draw_call
sites.patch: render_view: CALL sky_draw (0x41A4D0) -> CALL brr_hook_sky_draw: the view's camera and projection recorded, the bands drawn in the marker colour 255, and coloured as a smooth gradient when the frame is presented (sky.c); also where smooth shading (shade.c) starts each view

sites.name: fill_flat_smooth
sites.patch: fill_descriptors' smoothly lit flat-colour polygons (render flags 0x40, with and without depth): lighting set-up poly_light_smooth (0x446D70) -> brr_poly_light_smooth and spans span_gouraud_z (0x4438D0) / span_gouraud (0x443710) -> brr_span_gouraud_z / brr_span_gouraud (thunks.asm): the same pixels, plus each corner's shade fraction and each pixel's index and fraction for the full-colour picture (shade.c). Data, not code: the 3D engine reads the routines from here for every polygon

sites.name: fill_seethrough_smooth
sites.patch: fill_descriptors' see-through (checkerboard) polygons with smooth lighting: poly_light_smooth -> brr_poly_light_smooth; their stipple spans stay the game's

sites.name: fill_gouraud
sites.patch: fill_descriptors' Gouraud polygons (shades from the model): span_gouraud_z / span_gouraud -> our copies, as fill_flat_smooth; their lighting set-ups stay the game's

sites.name: render_view_entry
sites.patch: Experimental, [display] max_draw_distance above 0 only. render_view's first 6 instructions (PUSH EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI, EBP) -> JMP brr_hook_render_view + NOP: the view is drawn with vision distance (detail_level, 0x44B044) 25, the most the 64x64 visible-area grid holds (the game's limit is 22), and texture distance (0x44B048) max_draw_distance (the game's limit is 14); the player's values are put back afterwards; a trampoline repeats the PUSHes and continues at 0x4176CA

sites.name: landscape_walk_call
sites.patch: Experimental, [display] max_draw_distance 26-60 only. render_view: CALL 0x41D5E4 (the landscape walk) -> CALL brr_hook_landscape_walk: the walk with the vision distance at max_draw_distance (the flat squares' and the display list's fades), then distance.c's far passes: the squares beyond the near pass, in 61x61 windows of the 64x64 grid, each with the tables rebuilt by 0x41D24C (camera square shifted) and the walk's loop from 0x41D618

sites.name: music_check_call
sites.patch: WinMain: CALL 0x409F00 (the start-up music check, just after the DirectDraw set-up) -> CALL brr_hook_music_check, which puts our mciSendCommandA back in the import slot 0x56C160 (cnc-ddraw's hooks replace it during the set-up), then runs the check

protected_about: Game functions reachable from the race tick (direct calls, Phase 3 call graph) except approach_clamped and FUN_004274fc (the menus' mouse position, skipped in a race), which are patched on purpose. The DLL hashes them before and after patching.
